Android normally shows a “Start recording or casting?” dialog every time subtitles start. Advanced users can pre-approve it once via adb, so subtitles start instantly from then on:

1. Enable Developer options and USB debugging, connect your device to a computer with adb installed.

2. Run:

%1$s

That's it: the setting survives reboots, and you can turn USB debugging back off afterwards. The app itself doesn't change: Android just auto-grants the dialog.

To undo it:

%2$s

Note: this relies on undocumented Android behavior (the PROJECT_MEDIA app-op). On some devices (e.g. certain Xiaomi/Samsung builds) it may not work or may get reset by the system; the normal dialog is always the fallback.

Parakeet is the fast default for 25 European languages. Whisper covers more languages and can translate to English; larger Whisper models usually improve accuracy but use more memory and run slower. OSTT keeps ordinary dictation as one continuous utterance so pauses do not become false sentence boundaries. Whisper uses its native contextual windows; very long input for other offline families uses overlapping, reconciled windows. Specialist families may target particular languages or domains—check their source page. Size guide: under 128 MB is compact; 128–768 MB is phone-friendly; 768 MB–2 GB is demanding; over 2 GB is mainly for high-memory devices.

How to use it
• Open any app and tap the microphone on a supported keyboard/app. A small panel slides up, you speak, tap to stop, and the text is inserted. (Enable “Auto-stop after silence” in the settings to have it stop by itself.)

Which keyboards open the voice panel
• Microsoft SwiftKey (not open source) and website voice search open the panel directly.
• AnySoftKeyboard is the open-source way to get the panel: its mic key opens it as long as no voice keyboard is enabled on your system.

Other open-source keyboards
• HeliBoard, FlorisBoard, OpenBoard, Fossify Keyboard and Unexpected Keyboard don't open the panel: their mic key switches to the “Offline Speech to Text” keyboard instead. Enable it once under Setup → Voice keyboard, speak there, and use its keyboard-switch key to go back. FUTO Keyboard ships its own voice input.
• Gboard only uses Google's own voice typing and can't use this app at all.

If SwiftKey's own voice typing opens instead
• Settings → Rich input → turn off “Multi-modal voice typing”.
• Then tap the mic again and pick “Offline Speech to Text”.

If Android asks which app to use
• Choose “Offline Speech to Text” and tap “Always”.

If another app always opens instead
• Open Settings → Apps → that app → “Open by default” → Clear defaults, then try again.
